personas.name: Marketing operations
personas.pain: Fragmented enrichment and unclear MQL ownership
personas.promise: A source-linked signal, a shared qualification rule and a visible acceptance receipt.
personas.subject: A cleaner handoff from {{signal}}
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, your team’s interest in {{workflow}} suggests a specific place to start: one enrichment table, one agreed MQL rule and a clear owner. How do you currently tell whether those signals turn into meetings the SDR team accepts?
personas.question: How is MQL acceptance defined, and where does the feedback return?

personas.name: SDR leadership
personas.pain: High-volume queues that hide the reason to call
personas.promise: Prioritized context, an owner and a relevant opening for each accepted signal.
personas.subject: The reason to call {{account}}
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, the useful output of a buying signal is a conversation your team can act on. I’d like to understand how reps see the source, timing and next step today. Where does context tend to disappear between marketing and the SDR queue?
personas.question: Which rejection reasons would help Marketing improve the next cohort?

pitch: I bring the perspective of someone who has done the outbound work and now builds the systems behind it. My local partnership CRM preserves contact provenance, imports and pipeline stages; Hey Sammy turns scattered sources into structured records. At Clay, I would connect that building experience to MQL definitions, enrichment quality and the marketing-to-SDR handoff.
mappings: Hey Sammy: source evidence, validation, deduplication and resumable jobs.
Attach provenance to the field that changes the qualification decision.
SideQuest: local partnership CRM, imports, pipeline stages and campaign drafts.
Build one complete handoff with acceptance feedback.
Enterprise sales, startup messaging and outbound; 124% quota attainment.
Review whether a signal gives a rep a useful reason to call.
northStar: Accepted pipeline from a sourced signal
weekOne: A usable, sourced handoff for one marketing campaign.
days60: Expand the accepted-signal workflow to a second segment; compare enrichment cost, routing errors and meetings held.
days90: Use seller feedback and cohort outcomes to refine MQL definitions, lifecycle timing and campaign investment.

firstBuilds.title: Signal-to-SDR handoff
firstBuilds.goal: Make one intent source useful to an SDR without losing its evidence.
firstBuilds.scope: 50 historical signals, then one reviewed campaign.
firstBuilds.measure: Owner accuracy, time to acceptance, rejection reasons and meetings held.

firstBuilds.title: Enrichment efficiency
firstBuilds.goal: Spend credits on fields that change a GTM decision.
firstBuilds.scope: One account segment and a small provider comparison.
firstBuilds.measure: Verified fields per credit, stale fields and cost per accepted account.

firstBuilds.title: Campaign measurement
firstBuilds.goal: Join campaign activity to the handoff and opportunity.
firstBuilds.scope: One campaign with agreed definitions and an SDR feedback partner.
firstBuilds.measure: MQL → accepted → held → opportunity conversion by source.

projectRelevance.sammy: Source-backed discovery and validation translate directly to credible enrichment and buying-signal research.
projectRelevance.sidequest: The local partnership CRM and PostHog work connect clean records, campaign drafts and commercial measurement.
projectRelevance.dancers: Private inquiries and dependable follow-up are useful patterns for handoffs with clear ownership and recovery.
